title: Wallabies defeat Japan 56-17 in second Test
dek: Australia defeated Japan 56-17 in Townsville to secure three consecutive Test wins for the first time since 2024 under new coach Les Kiss. The Wallabies trailed at halftime before dominating the second half through set piece and breakdown work.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Australia 56, Japan 17 final score in Townsville
bottom_line: Australia's second-half dominance erased early vulnerability and extended the winning streak to three Tests. Watch whether this level of second-half control repeats in the Nations Championship, or whether the prior week's 'scratchy outing' remains the recurring pattern under Kiss.
body: Australia defeated Japan 56-17 in the second Test in Townsville, according to ESPN's reporting. The Wallabies secured three consecutive Test wins for the first time since 2024 under new coach Les Kiss.

The margin masked a tighter first half. Australia trailed before Taniela Tupou scored his second try to give the hosts a 21-17 halftime lead. In the second half, the Wallabies' set piece and breakdown work dominated, with forwards scoring close-range tries to build the 39-point margin.

This win was described as a perfect response after what Kiss' opening Test the previous week had been characterized as a scratchy performance. The second-half execution demonstrated the structure Les Kiss' tenure is intended to build.

Japan's opening innings in the match kept the contest competitive through the first 40 minutes. The hosts' collapse in the second half points to execution gaps rather than tactical imbalance once Australia found its rhythm.

The brief does not detail other try scorers beyond Tupou, specific dates, or how this result positions the Wallabies within the Nations Championship standings. The open questions around the exact composition of the three-match winning streak and whether this result affects playoff positioning remain unaddressed by the source.
